claims.text: The local Japanese pre-English catalog models Expansion Sheet Series 1 Blue / 拡張シート 第1弾 青版 with a March 23, 1998 release date.
The local release file models 36 strict-member rows for Expansion Sheet Series 1 Blue.
The local release identifies the product as glossy Vending/Expansion Sheet cards, with Pokellector as the primary source and Bulbapedia card-page caption metadata used for artist-credit texture.

The pre-English symbol-status matrix marks Expansion Sheet Series 1 Blue as prints_without_rarity_symbol: no, high confidence, with trap consequence that vending cards are glossy and not the Base No Rarity lane.

Series 1 Blue matters because it is Pokemon memory in a vending-sheet body: familiar Kanto faces, common rarity signals, glossy physical format, and a dense artist roster make distribution form part of identity.

The local file surfaces a dense artist roster including Atsuko Nishida, Aya Kusube, Mitsuhiro Arita, Kagemaru Himeno, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, Tomokazu Komiya, Ken Sugimori, Ai Kurihara, Yuuki Kawamura, Kasumi Matsuda, Craig Turvey, and Keiji Kinebuchi, with credits scoped to catalog/provider metadata.
This tranche hand-authors the queue chases Pikachu 019, Mewtwo 022, and Chansey 031, plus starter/object/artist-anchor rows that teach vending-sheet identity across the release.

narrative.human_title: Expansion Sheet Series 1 Blue — glossy vending memory, not pack memory
narrative.why_it_matters: Series 1 Blue is where early Pokemon feels like it came out of a machine with a shine on it. The names are familiar, but the assembly is different: vending sheet, glossy stock, common rarity, row-number discipline, and a crowded artist bench. It is beautiful because it refuses the easy shortcut from famous character to familiar set.
